title: VUA packages-ops result v0.5
description: Result documents for the packages-ops v0.5 write face slice A5 = project creation (proposal 026 freeze batch 2026-09-19; the v0.1 A1 removal result row, the v0.2 A2 install/upgrade result row, the v0.3 A3 registration result row and the v0.4 A4 repository add/remove result row stay frozen and served untouched). Envelope mirrors the standing wire shape (schemaVersion/operation/result); the envelope const is the word-list-row family version 0.5 and the result document carries its own family const vua.packages-ops/v0.5 — the two versions are independent (the c914cf2 standing rule). Operation/kind lock extended to nine methods: BOTH preview methods are synchronous queries and answer kind=plan exactly (their failures are wire-envelope errors, not result arms); the apply methods, the A3 registration, ALL THREE A4 methods and the A5 creation are nine-state tasks whose terminal reflux answers kind=receipt / kind=rejected / kind=registered / kind=repoReceipt / kind=created respectively. kind=created (projectCreated) is the A5 receipt — THE FIRST PACKAGES-OPS RECEIPT WITH AN ACTUAL-RESULT PAYLOAD: the create_project port answers Result<ProjectRef, _> (unlike the unit-answering A3/A4 faces), so the receipt carries the ProjectRef projection {projectId, projectPath} — projectId = the port ProjectRef.id echo (an informational creation fact minted by the backend; NOT the 013 project identity key, the project identity stays the path) and projectPath = the port ProjectRef.root echo (the new project's root directory = its registered-project path identity; the registered-project list shows the project on next refresh — the REGISTERS-IN-STORE side effect is the frozen port fact: both backends' success paths tail-call FileSystemProjectStore::initialize, so a created project IS a registered project; the word face never invents a 'directory-only, unregistered' shape). additionalProperties:false forbids inventing more (no created-at timestamps, no template-copy stats, no package lists). Key set disjoint from every prior receipt arm. kind=rejected: the typed guard refusal evaluated INSIDE the task; the guard closed set stands at the A1/A2 three values — A5 adds NO guard: creation refusals are backend answers and every one folds into execution_failed carrying the ORIGINAL port code inside detail as honest provenance (the A1/A2/A3/A4 discipline). THE A5 PORT-CODE CLOSED SET IS THREE EXISTING CODES, ZERO NEW (the port method and both implementations predate this batch — the freeze transports their honest faces, it mints no code): vua.vpm.template_missing (the library-path carrier for ALL FOUR i18n message keys — errors.vpm.projectExists / errors.vpm.projectNameInvalid / errors.vpm.templateMissing / errors.vpm.templateCopyFailed share this one code with per-key categories Validation/Validation/Dependency/ExternalFailure: the i18n message key and the port error code are TWO layers and the wire face declares both honestly), vua.vpm.apply_failed (the VCC CLI path: timeout or non-zero vpm new exit carrying the exitCode, and the store-initialize leg), vua.vpm.backend_unavailable (the VCC CLI runner-spawn failure — a shape the library path never answers). THE TWO BACKENDS' REFUSAL SHAPES DIFFER and the protocol document declares the difference — no unified shape is invented. The rejected code pattern stays locked to ^vua\.packages\. — the reused vua.vpm.* codes never travel inside a rejected document. Capability absence never reaches a task: the wire gate answers the generic capability_missing as an envelope error before submit (the gate reads the EXISTING five-bit VpmCapabilities.create_project face — no new accessor on this batch). additionalProperties:false everywhere is the false-assertion guard: facts with no port carrier (creation timestamps, copy byte counts, template resolution traces) are INVALID by schema, not merely discouraged.

packageId.description: The VPM package identifier (the manifest name). No tighter pattern is frozen: the word list transports facts, it does not re-litigate upstream id grammar.

version.description: Target version for installs; null for removals (port fact: Option, verbatim).

reason.description: Machine reason, e.g. transitive_dependency, conflict; null when the backend carries none (port fact: Option, verbatim).

items.description: Every change the request would make (ORC-WF-002: the plan must cover every change the backend will make). On the install face this includes transitive dependency installs and conflict-triggered remove rows.

conflicts.description: Free-text machine reasons for dependency breakage the change would cause — the transparency face; the confirm UI must warn, the authoritative verdict stays server-side.

destructive.description: True when the change set contains conflicts or legacy removals (ADR-0006) — the confirm UI must warn; a false assertion is checkable against the other four faces.

digest.description: FNV-1a over the canonical item list; the applyInstall confirmedDigest binds to exactly this value. NOTE (consumer narrowing): the v0.1/v0.2/v0.3/v0.4/v0.5 plan shapes share the same key set — narrow by the schemaVersion literal, not by keys alone.

confirmedDigest.description: The digest the user confirmed, echoed — the audit link between the confirmation face and the executed result.

requestedPackageIds.description: The explicit request list, verbatim — the change list half of the audit receipt (the A1 removal variant; key set disjoint from installReceipt, registerReceipt, the A4 arms and the A5 created arm).

removedItems.description: What the backend actually removed (port apply_remove {removed: items} verbatim) — the actual-result half of the audit receipt.

confirmedDigest.description: The digest the user confirmed, echoed — the audit link between the confirmation face and the executed result.

version.description: The request's version-selection fact, verbatim: null = resolver-picked, a string = the pin.

requestedPackages.description: The explicit request rows, verbatim (version-selection semantics included) — the change list half of the audit receipt (the A2 install variant; key set disjoint from removeReceipt, registerReceipt, the A4 arms and the A5 created arm).

appliedItems.description: What the backend actually applied (port apply_install {applied: items} verbatim) — the actual-result half of the audit receipt. No minimum is invented: an honestly empty array transports as an empty array.

packageRoot.description: The request's packageRoot, echoed — the only fact the face has (the port answers Result<(), _>: no applied/removed payload exists, and the idempotent AlreadyAdded collapse means there is no first-vs-repeat fact either; additionalProperties:false forbids inventing one). Key set disjoint from removeReceipt, installReceipt, the A4 arms and the A5 created arm.

url.description: The request's url, echoed — the audit fact (the port answers Result<(), _>: no payload exists; additionalProperties:false forbids inventing more). Key set disjoint from localRepoAdded, repoRemoved, projectCreated and every prior receipt arm.

path.description: The request's path, echoed — the audit fact (the port answers Result<(), _>: no payload exists; additionalProperties:false forbids inventing more). Key set disjoint from remoteRepoAdded, repoRemoved, projectCreated and every prior receipt arm.

repoId.description: The removed row's repository id, echoed — the one fact the face has (the port answers Result<(), _>: the id is already the request's identifying fact, the echo IS the audit link; no removed-row snapshot is invented — a row may carry absent-id facts this face never round-trips). Key set disjoint from remoteRepoAdded, localRepoAdded, projectCreated and every prior receipt arm.

projectId.description: The port ProjectRef.id, echoed verbatim — the creation fact the backend minted (an informational identifier; NOT the 013 project identity key: the project identity stays the path). The ONE packages-ops receipt with an actual-result payload: the create_project port answers Result<ProjectRef, _>, and this key set is exactly that projection's first half. Key set disjoint from every prior receipt arm.

projectPath.description: The port ProjectRef.root, echoed verbatim — the new project's root directory, identical to its registered-project path identity: the REGISTERS-IN-STORE side effect is the frozen port fact (both backends' success paths tail-call FileSystemProjectStore::initialize), so a created project IS a registered project and the registered-project list shows it on next refresh (no 'directory-only, unregistered' shape is invented). Key set disjoint from every prior receipt arm.

detail.description: Free-text provenance. On the A5 face every port refusal folds here with the ORIGINAL port code carried verbatim (vua.vpm.template_missing — the library-path carrier for all four i18n message keys projectExists/projectNameInvalid/templateMissing/templateCopyFailed; vua.vpm.apply_failed — the VCC CLI timeout/non-zero-exit and store-initialize legs carrying the exitCode; vua.vpm.backend_unavailable — the VCC CLI runner-spawn failure) plus the reason — the reused vua.vpm.* codes never travel in the code key (the 013 reuse-code law: the pattern above stays locked to the vua.packages. family). The two backends' refusal shapes differ and the protocol document declares the difference; no unified shape is invented.
